Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Let $C$ be a free based chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with integer bifiltration $(i,j)$, multiplication by $U$ lowering both coordinates by one, and differential not increasing either coordinate. Chains have finite support. The filtration of a sum is the maximum of the coordinates of its supported basis monomials. Write $V=C\{i=0\}$ and, for an integer $s$, write $E_s=C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ and $A_s=C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$. These are the subquotients supported on the vertical line, the northeast hook, and the southwest hook respectively. More precisely, $V=C\{i\le0\}/C\{i<0\}$; $E_s$ is the subcomplex supported on $i=0$ or $j=s$ in the quotient $C/C\{i<0\text{ or }j<s\}$; and $A_s=C\{i\le0,j\le s\}/C\{i<0,j<s\}$. Define $F_s:H(V)\to H(E_s)$ by quotienting the vertical line below $s$ and including the resulting upper ray into $E_s$. Define $G_s:H(A_s)\to H(V)$ by killing the strictly left ray and including the resulting lower vertical ray.

If a class $\xi\in H(V)$ has a cycle representative supported at $j\le s$ and satisfies $F_s(\xi)=0$, then $\xi$ belongs to the image of $G_s$. Consequently, if $H(V)$ is one-dimensional and $s$ is the least level representing its nonzero class, the two maps $F_s,G_s$ cannot both be zero.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Let $\mathcal R$ consist of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}v^\alpha$ over $\mathbb F_2$, where $S$ is a well-ordered subset of $[0,\infty)$, including the empty support. Addition is coefficientwise and multiplication is convolution of exponents. These operations are well-defined and make $\mathcal R$ a commutative integral domain. Allowing well-ordered supports in all of $\mathbb R$ gives a field $\mathcal K$ containing $\mathcal R$. Every nonzero element of either ring is uniquely of the form $v^\alpha(1+h)$, where $\alpha$ is its least exponent and $h$ has strictly positive well-ordered support. The factor $1+h$ is a unit of $\mathcal R$. Consequently $\mathcal K$ is the field of fractions of $\mathcal R$, and $\mathcal R$ is its valuation ring: a nonzero series belongs to $\mathcal R$ exactly when its least exponent is nonnegative.

Let $\mathcal R$ be the nonnegative real-exponent series ring over $\mathbb F_2$, with $\operatorname{gr}(v^\alpha)=-\alpha$. Let $C$ be a finite free $\mathcal R$-module with a fixed finite real-graded basis and an $\mathcal R$-linear differential of degree $-1$. Then graded changes of basis decompose $C$ into finitely many zero-differential rank-one summands and finitely many two-term summands
$$\mathcal R x\xrightarrow{\partial}\mathcal R y,\qquad\partial x=v^\alpha y,\quad\partial y=0,\quad\alpha\ge0.$$
Consequently homology is a finite direct sum of graded copies of $\mathcal R$ and of cyclic torsion modules $\mathcal R/(v^\alpha)$; a summand with $\alpha=0$ contributes zero homology. If there is a non-torsion homology class, the maximal grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class exists and equals the greatest grading of the finitely many free homology generators.

The **grid-complex algorithm** takes a finite encoded grid and a mode from $\{\mathrm{tilde},\mathrm{minus\text{-}associated\text{-}graded},\mathrm{minus\text{-}filtered}\}$. It requires an integer grid number $n\ge2$, disjoint $O$- and $X$-markings with exactly one of each in every row and column, and an induced component permutation that is one $n$-cycle. If $n<2$ or the marking conditions fail, return `invalid-grid`; if the component permutation has more than one cycle, return `link-input-not-supported`. No chain complex is returned on either branch.

For a valid knot grid, number the horizontal and vertical circles $1,\ldots,n$ and enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ in lexicographic order. The state for a permutation $\sigma$ consists of the $n$ intersections $(i,\sigma(i))$. For each ordered pair of states $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$, if they agree in other than exactly $n-2$ points, add no rectangle terms. Otherwise enumerate the at most two torus rectangles with the four nonshared state points as corners, retain those whose interiors contain no point of $\mathbf x$, and apply the selected mode. In the full filtered mode, each term drops filtration by $n_{\mathbb X}(r)$; the associated-graded mode retains precisely the terms with zero drop, which are the rectangles with no $X$-marking:

1. **Tilde mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2$. Count a retained rectangle with coefficient $1$ exactly when its interior contains no $O$- or $X$-marking.
2. **Associated-graded minus mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each $U_i$ of Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$. Count a retained rectangle exactly when its interior contains no $X$-marking, with coefficient $\prod_{i=1}^n U_i^{O_i(r)}$.
3. **Full filtered minus mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each $U_i$ of Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$. Count every retained rectangle, regardless of its $X$-markings, with coefficient $\prod_{i=1}^n U_i^{O_i(r)}$. Use the grid Alexander value for each state and assign filtration drop $n_{\mathbb X}(r)$ to this term.

Return the ordered state list, the mode and coefficient ring, the exact differential matrix obtained by summing coefficients modulo two, the state Maslov and Alexander values, and the filtration data for the full filtered mode. The algorithm returns this finite presentation only; its identification with knot Floer homology and its independence of the chosen grid are separate theorems. The factor $V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ is not multiplied into the output.

The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. Assume countable choice. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. $$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. $$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot smoothly concordant to the unknot. Then there are finite-rank free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ bifiltered chain complexes $A$ and $B$, each having zero total homology, such that
$$ \mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A\simeq \Lambda\oplus B, $$
where $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ is the normalized unknot complex with zero differential and generator in Maslov grading and both filtration coordinates zero, and $\simeq$ is a Maslov-graded filtered chain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies do not increase either filtration. The acyclic summands are acyclic only after the filtrations are forgotten; no acyclicity of their associated-graded complexes is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

$$ \tau(C)=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z: H_*(C\{i=0,j\le s\})\longrightarrow H_*(C\{i=0\})\text{ is nonzero} \}. $$
For each integer $s$, let $F_s$ be the homology map induced by the chain map from $C\{i=0\}$ to $C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i=0,j<s\}$ and then including the quotient. Let $G_s$ be the homology map from $C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$ to $C\{i=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i<0,j=s\}$ and then including. The epsilon invariant is
$$ \epsilon(C)=\begin{cases} 1,&F_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ -1,&G_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ 0,&F_{\tau(C)}\ne0\text{ and }G_{\tau(C)}\ne0. \end{cases} $$
Here zero and nonzero refer to the induced homology maps. This definition fixes the sign convention; invariance under stable equivalence is a separate claim.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Work over $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. Let $C,D$ be finite-rank free Maslov-graded, integer-bifiltered complexes with homogeneous bifiltered bases, differential of degree $-1$ not increasing either coordinate, and $U$ of degree $(-2,-1,-1)$ in Maslov and the two filtration coordinates. Suppose $H(C)\cong H(D)\cong\Lambda$ with generator in Maslov degree zero and $H(C\{i=0\})\cong H(D\{i=0\})\cong\mathbb F_2$. If $C\oplus A$ and $D\oplus B$ are Maslov-graded bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent for arbitrary Maslov-graded bifiltered $\Lambda$-complexes $A,B$ with zero total homology, using $\Lambda$-linear maps and homotopies of the stated grading and filtration degrees, then $\tau(C)=\tau(D)$, and the homology maps $F_\tau,G_\tau$ in the epsilon definition have the same zero/nonzero patterns for $C,D$. Consequently their epsilon values agree whenever those three-case values are defined. No finite rank, freeness, vertical, horizontal, or associated-graded acyclicity of the added complexes $A,B$ is required, and epsilon is not being defined on the stabilized complexes.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every valid connected one-component
oriented code with a selected outer face, the reconstruction procedure
produces a regular oriented diagram representing that code. Any two such
diagrams with the same code differ only by crossing and edge relabeling and
are planar isotopic. The normalized planar-diagram code of a diagram with $c$
crossings appears among the candidates enumerated at bound $c$. This statement
concerns diagrams and their finite codes; it does not identify distinct codes
that may represent the same knot type. The finite realization and enumeration
claims are choice-free; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is assumed only for the smooth
ambient-isotopy uniqueness clause.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Identify the standard oriented three-sphere with $S^3=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1\}$ and choose $0<r<1$. The standard unknotted Heegaard torus is $T_r=\{|z_1|=r,\ |z_2|=\sqrt{1-r^2}\}$; its two sides are solid tori. In the angular coordinates $(u,v)\in(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^2$ given by $(u,v)\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i u},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i v})$, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the first and second coordinate classes in $H_1(T_r;\mathbb Z)$. For coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, the **oriented torus knot** $T(p,q)$ is the image of $s\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i p s},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i q s})$, for $s\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, oriented by increasing $s$; it represents the primitive slope $p\alpha+q\beta$. The mirror convention is the reflection $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(z_1,\overline{z_2})$, which sends $T(p,q)$ to $T(p,-q)$ with image orientation, and reversing the knot orientation gives $T(-p,-q)$. For nonzero $p,q$ with $d=\gcd(|p|,|q|)>1$, the corresponding torus link is the union of $d$ disjoint parallel copies of the primitive slope $(p/d,q/d)$; it is not a single embedded curve of class $p\alpha+q\beta$. The exterior is $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ for a chosen closed tubular neighborhood. A positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and a preferred longitude is a degree-one class on $\partial E_K$ whose image in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is zero; this definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

Let $P$ be the projection plane in an oriented $3$-sphere and let $n$ be the
unit viewing normal pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ so that $(u,v)$ is
a positive basis exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive ambient basis. A
**crossing code** has a
finite set $C$ of crossing labels and a finite set $D$ of **darts**, where a
dart is one directed half-edge incident to a crossing. A fixed-point-free
involution $\alpha:D\to D$ pairs the two ends of each edge: $\alpha^2=\mathrm{id}$
and $\alpha(d)\ne d$. A vertex map $v:D\to C$ records the crossing incident to
each dart. A **rotation system** is the permutation $\sigma$ whose cycles give
the clockwise order of darts at each crossing. Each crossing has four darts;
the two over-strand darts and the two under-strand darts are opposite in that
cyclic order. An arrow on each dart records whether its edge is directed into
or out of its incident crossing. The pairing $\alpha$ must join one incoming
end to one outgoing end. At a crossing, each opposite pair has one incoming
and one outgoing dart, so following an edge and then the opposite dart defines
the oriented link components. A code is **connected** when the graph with
vertices $C$ and edges the $\alpha$-pairs is connected.

The sign of an oriented crossing is $+1$ or $-1$ according as
$\det(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ is positive or negative, where the two
tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. This item fixes
the local cyclic-order convention as follows. Starting with the outgoing
over-dart and reading counterclockwise, a positive crossing has order
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm out},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm in})$; a negative crossing has
order $(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$. The stored crossing
sign and cyclic order must agree. This is the page's explicit sign convention.
It agrees with the current KT-03 supplier: reversing its positive
counterclockwise order from outgoing over gives the clockwise record
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$.

For a nonempty connected crossing graph, let $V=|C|$, $E=|D|/2$, and let
$F$ be the number of cycles of the face permutation $\phi=\alpha\circ\sigma$.
A **spherical code** is a code satisfying $V-E+F=2$. A spherical code becomes a
**plane code** by distinguishing one face as the outer face and deleting a
point in that face from the sphere. The crossingless one-component code is a separate case: its Gauss data are one empty component word, its DT pairing and crossing-sign vector are empty at $c=0$, and its PD data are the single loop `Loop[1]`; every format also carries an orientation marker, `ccw` or `cw`, for the unit circle $S^1=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$ in the oriented plane, and the outer-face marker is `outside`. Thus the crossingless code records which direction orients its circle. It has no crossing graph or face-permutation test. Disconnected crossing graphs and disconnected crossingless links are outside this code class.

A **normalized planar-diagram code** with $c>0$ has crossing labels
$C=\{1,\ldots,c\}$ and four dart positions $0,1,2,3$ at each crossing, in
clockwise order beginning with the outgoing over-dart. The opposite pair
$(0,2)$ is over and $(1,3)$ is under. For sign $+1$, the clockwise record is
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$; for sign $-1$ it is
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm out},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm in})$. Edge labels are assigned
by scanning crossings in increasing order and their four dart positions in
order, giving the next positive integer to the pair containing the first
not-yet-labelled dart. The outer face is recorded by its least dart in its
face cycle. These rules remove arbitrary edge-name and face-name choices;
different crossing labelings may still represent the same diagram. At $c=0$
a normalized code is the crossingless record with one of the two orientation
markers above.

A **Gauss code** for an oriented diagram records, in traversal order on each
oriented component, a signed crossing label: $+j$ means the component passes
over at crossing $j$, and $-j$ means it passes under. For a knot there is one
cyclic word; for a link there is one cyclic word per component. Each crossing
label must occur exactly twice in total, once positively and once negatively.
When $c>0$, every listed component word is nonempty; a separate crossingless
component is not part of this code class. The zero-crossing case is only the
one-component code specified above.
The code also carries a separate algebraic crossing-sign vector
$\varepsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$, one entry for each label. Choosing a basepoint
turns the knot's cyclic word into a based word; changing the basepoint
cyclically shifts the word, and relabeling crossings changes only their names.
The visit order, over/under signs, and crossing-sign vector determine the
crossing rotation system; it is realizable in the sphere only when the
resulting code is spherical. A plane Gauss code also carries an identifier of
one cycle of its face permutation to designate the outer face.

A **signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite code**, in this page's convention, encodes a
based oriented knot with $c$ crossings by numbering its $2c$ visits
$1,\ldots,2c$ in traversal order. For each odd visit $2j-1$, record the even
visit $2k$ paired with it as $d_j=+2k$ when the odd visit is over and
$d_j=-2k$ when it is under; also record the algebraic crossing sign
$\varepsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$ for crossing label $j$, the pair containing odd
visit $2j-1$. Its parity conditions are that
$|d_1|,\ldots,|d_c|$ are exactly the even numbers $2,4,\ldots,2c$, each once,
and each paired crossing has one over-visit and one under-visit. The separate
$\varepsilon_j$ records the crossing sign; signed DT conventions elsewhere
may encode signs differently. The associated cyclic traversal and crossing
signs determine a rotation system, which must pass the same spherical
realizability test. A plane DT code also carries an identifier of one cycle
of its face permutation to designate the outer face.

An **oriented planar-diagram code** labels each edge segment by an integer and
lists its two incident darts at crossing records. Each crossing record lists
its four directed edge ends in clockwise order, beginning with the outgoing
over-dart, and records which opposite pair is over, the orientation of each
strand, and the crossing sign. Every edge label occurs exactly twice, once as
an incoming end and once as an outgoing end. The code must satisfy the local
crossing-order rule above; its crossing graph must be connected when nonempty;
and its rotation system must satisfy $V-E+F=2$. The record also carries an
identifier of one cycle of its face permutation as the outer face. Thus an
arbitrary word in labels, even when each label occurs twice, is not declared
realizable until all incidence, orientation, crossing, connectedness, and
face-count tests pass.

derivations.claim: In the finite-rank free Maslov-graded knot Floer category, [F4] proves the stable-equivalence conclusion directly. Its finite endomorphism matrices strictify homotopy idempotents and give a unique non-acyclic indecomposable core up to filtered homotopy. The rank-one vertical homology of each original knot complex forces its internal acyclic complementary summands to have acyclic vertical complexes. Consequently its vertical threshold and the zero/nonzero patterns of $F_\tau,G_\tau$ are precisely those of that core. Stable equivalence identifies the two cores even if the externally added acyclic summands have nonzero vertical or associated-graded homology. Thus the three-case epsilon values in [F1] agree. This argument does not apply the epsilon definition to the stabilized complexes themselves.

First reduce a finite based Laurent complex by explicit filtered contractions. If a differential coefficient preserves both coordinates, homogeneity makes it a single Laurent monomial; translate its target so that it is $1$. Write $da=b+r$ with $a,b$ at the same bifiltration and replace $b$ by $b'=da$. This is a filtered homogeneous basis change with inverse $b=b'+r$. For every other basis element $c$, subtract the coefficient of $b'$ in $dc$ times $a$ from $c$; this is filtered since the relevant copy of $a$ has the coordinates of the corresponding copy of $b'$. The new differentials contain no $b'$, and their $a$ coefficients vanish by $d^2=0$. Thus the pair $a\to b'$ splits off. Inclusion $I$, projection $P$ and $H(b')=a$, zero on all other generators, satisfy $PI=1$ and $IP+1=dH+Hd$, with $H$ preserving both filtrations and of Maslov degree $+1$. Finitely many repetitions give a reduced complex with no equal-bifiltration arrow. Tensoring these identities with another complex preserves them: the extra differential terms cancel over $\mathbb F_2$. Dualizing likewise preserves them. This supplies all reduction inverse maps and homotopies used below, including their tensor compatibility.

Let $s=\tau(C)$ and choose a Maslov-zero vertical cycle $z$ at $j\le s$ representing its distinguished class. Its corner part $z_c$ is nonzero, or the threshold would be smaller. If $F_s=0$, choose a Maslov-one northeast-hook chain $b$ with $d_Nb=z_c$ and split it into strictly upper, corner and strictly right parts $b_+,b_0,b_r$. The strictly upper part of $d_vb_+$ is zero, since the other parts cannot reach it. Hence $z'=z+d_vb_+$ is another distinguished vertical cycle supported at $j\le s$. Put $q=b_0+b_r$. Its horizontal boundary $h=d_hq$ has no strictly right component, and its corner is $z'_c$, by the corner equation of $d_Nb=z_c$. Then $x=z'+h_{\mathrm{left}}$ is supported in $i\le0,j\le s$, its vertical projection represents the distinguished class, and its horizontal projection is the boundary $h$. Conversely, if such an $x$ has horizontal part $d_hq$, project $q$ to the northeast hook: its strictly left part cannot reach the corner or right ray, and the remaining boundary is precisely $x_c$, with no upper component. Thus $F_s=0$. This proves the exact boundary-representative alternative, rather than assuming a simultaneous simplification theorem.

If $G_s
e0$, choose a Maslov-zero southwest-hook cycle mapping to the distinguished vertical class. In the reduced complex it is $x=z+\ell$, with $z$ on the lower vertical ray, including the corner, and $\ell$ strictly left at $j=s$. The two retained boundary equations are exactly $d_vz=0$ and $d_h(z_c+\ell)=0$: a lower ray cannot reach the other ray, and the corner has no equal-bifiltration differential. Conversely these two equations give a southwest-hook cycle mapping to the vertical class. Therefore $G_s
e0$ is exactly the existence of this simultaneous vertical/horizontal cycle representative. If also $F_s
e0$, its horizontal cycle is not a boundary, by step 2.1. Each constructed $x$ extends to a homogeneous filtered Laurent basis: choose a nonzero original corner coordinate $e$, whose coefficient is $1$, and replace $e$ by $x$. Homogeneity excludes any other power of that same basis element, and all other terms are no higher in either filtration, so the inverse is the same filtered elementary substitution. These are the needed distinguished representative normal forms. A chosen horizontal noncycle alone is not used as an epsilon test.

The dual vertical threshold is $-s$. Indeed, if $B$ is the vertical boundary space, the distinguished cycle $z$ is not in $B+V^{\le s-1}$, since such an expression would give a lower-level cycle representing it. Finite-dimensional basis extension gives a cocycle functional annihilating that subspace and taking $z$ to $1$; its dual filtration is at most $-s$. A dual cocycle at level at most $-s-1$ vanishes on every cycle at level $s$ and hence on the one-dimensional vertical homology, so it is a dual boundary. The finite perfect pairing identifies the dual of the northeast hook at $s$ with the southwest hook of $C^*$ at $-s$. The transpose of $F_s(C)$ is $G_{-s}(C^*)$, and the transpose of $G_s(C)$ is $F_{-s}(C^*)$: quotient/inclusion maps reverse under this pairing. Duality of finite-dimensional homology preserves zero/nonzero. Thus $\epsilon(C^*)=-\epsilon(C)$; [F2] identifies this with $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$.

Normalize Laurent bases at $i=0$. The vertical slice of $C\otimes D$ is the ordinary field tensor of the vertical slices, with differential $d_v\otimes1+1\otimes d_v$; no term lowering algebraic level can survive there. Similarly horizontal slices at levels $s,t$ tensor to the horizontal slice at $s+t$. Splitting a finite field complex into boundary pairs and homology representatives proves the field Kunneth assertion directly: a boundary pair tensored with anything is contractible by its pair homotopy. In particular the tensor of distinguished vertical cycles represents the distinguished tensor class. Its threshold is $s+t$ by [F3]. All representatives used in steps 2.1, 3.1 are supported southwest, so their vertical and horizontal projections tensor exactly to the projections of their tensor.

We next admit the actual complexes used for the geometric examples. Use the following marking-cell arrays, rows ordered bottom to top: for positive $T_{2,5}$ take $n=7$, $O=[6,5,4,3,2,1,0]$, $X=[4,3,2,1,0,6,5]$; for positive $T_{4,5}$ take $n=9$, $O=[8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0]$, $X=[4,3,2,1,0,8,7,6,5]$. The first has five positive crossings and oriented over/under word $A^+B^-C^+D^-E^+A^-B^+C^-D^+E^-$, where superscripts indicate over/under and all crossing signs are positive. The explicit positive torus curve $(r e^{2it},s e^{5it})$, $r=s=1/\sqrt2$, has this identical code in stereographic projection: its planar angle is $2t$, radius $r/(1-s\sin5t)$, height $s\cos5t/(1-s\sin5t)$, and crossing parameters $t/(2\pi)=0,1/10,\ldots,9/10$. Equal projections force parameter difference $\pi$ and $\sin5t=0$. At the overparameter the radial derivative is positive and at the underpartner negative, so the oriented crossing determinant is positive. The angular derivative is nonzero, and there are no triple points. Thus [F6] admits this grid as the actual positive $T_{2,5}$.

Following oriented strands in the nine-grid gives fifteen positive crossings and the full signed rotation/strand code of the closure of the four-strand positive word $121321321121321$, after a cyclic starting-point change and reversal of the knot orientation. This is an explicit finite code equality: enumerate crossings in each row and column interval, then follow each row $O\to X$ and column $X\to O$; on the braid follow the strand permutation through each listed crossing, taking the top-right strand over to bottom-left. The exact words and crossing correspondence are recorded in the finite certificate named in Remarks. Commutations $13=31$ and braid relations $121=212$, $232=323$ give the successive words $123121321121321$, $123123121121321$, $123123121212321$, $123123121213231$, $123123121231231$, $123123121231213$, $123123121232123$, $123123121323123$, $123123123123123$. Each is a local disjoint-strand isotopy or oriented R3, so their closures are equivalent. The last is $(123)^5$. To identify its torus embedding, cut the Clifford curve $(r e^{4it},s e^{5it})$ by the disk coordinate $\arg(z_1)=\theta$: its four disk points have arguments $5(\theta+2\pi k)/4$. A generic phase makes one quarter-turn's braid $132$, which becomes $321$ by moving the first generator past the closure cut, and then $123$ by reversing the four disk positions via the half-turn conjugation. Five quarter-turns give the last closure. Finally simultaneous complex conjugation is an ambient SO(4) isotopy endpoint and sends this curve to its orientation reverse: rotate its two imaginary axes through $\pi$. Thus the code reversal preserves oriented knot type, and [F6] proves the actual positive $T_{4,5}$ admission.

Verify the trefoil grid in [F6] directly. Use row indices $0,1,2,3,4$ from bottom to top and column indices from left to right, as in [[def-grid-diagram-for-an-oriented-knot]], and draw the standard planar grid realization using the in-square mark-to-mark intervals. Following the grid orientation gives the single cycle $$O_{0,4}\to X_{0,2}\to O_{2,2}\to X_{2,0}\to O_{4,0}\to X_{4,3}\to O_{1,3}\to X_{1,1}\to O_{3,1}\to X_{3,4}\to O_{0,4}.$$ The horizontal and vertical intervals meet away from their endpoints at exactly three crossings: $c_1=(\text{row }1,\text{column }2)$, $c_2=(\text{row }2,\text{column }1)$, and $c_3=(\text{row }3,\text{column }3)$. Traversing the component from $O_{0,4}$ encounters $c_1$ over, $c_2$ under, $c_3$ over, $c_1$ under, $c_2$ over, and $c_3$ under. At $c_1$ and $c_2$ the oriented projected tangents $(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ are $((0,1),(-1,0))$; at $c_3$ they are $((0,-1),(1,0))$. Each determinant is $+1$ by [[def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes]]. Thus its signed oriented Gauss code is $1_O,2_U,3_O,1_U,2_O,3_U$ with crossing-sign vector $(+1,+1,+1)$. This code is also obtained by traversing the closure of the positive two-strand braid $\sigma_1^3$: its first braid strand encounters the three positive half twists over, under, over, and the returning strand encounters them under, over, under. The signed visit data determine the same crossing rotation and strand code, hence identify the face-permutation cycles. Retain the grid diagram's outer-face cycle and choose the corresponding face of the braid-closure diagram. To make this chosen face outer, compactify the projection plane to the oriented sphere $S^2$ and choose a point $q$ in that face, away from the diagram. An orientation-preserving rotation of $S^2$ sending $q$ to the projection point at infinity makes precisely this face outer. Realize the diagram lift in a product collar of the equatorial $S^2$ in $S^3$; the rotation extends by the same rotation on the first three coordinates and the identity on the normal coordinate. Its path of rotations is an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy of $S^3$ preserving the crossing heights and oriented strand data. The two resulting plane codes now have the same selected outer face, so [[thm-valid-code-reconstructs-the-declared-link-diagram]] identifies their diagrams up to planar isotopy. Thus the original grid and braid closure represent the same oriented knot even if their initially chosen planar outer faces differ. The braid closure lies on the standard unknotted torus with slope $2\alpha+3\beta$ (equivalently the swapped slope $3\alpha+2\beta$ under the orientation-preserving torus-coordinate swap), so it is $T(2,3)$ by [[def-coprime-torus-knot]]. The grid therefore represents the right-handed trefoil with its positive orientation, and its writhe is $+3$.

For the cable take $n=10$, $O=[8,9,7,6,4,5,3,2,1,0]$, $X=[4,5,2,3,0,1,8,9,6,7]$. Here is an explicit preferred-framing admission independent of any Floer calculation. Double each row and column of the admitted positive trefoil five-grid in [F6]. At an old corner let $h,v\in\{\pm1\}$ be the directions toward its horizontal and vertical partner. A diagonal two-mark block for $hv=1$ and an antidiagonal block for $hv=-1$ give exactly two crossing-free parallel corners; checking the four quadrants verifies this and the oriented attachments. Only at the $O$ corner $(\text{row }0,\text{column }4)$, where $h=-1,v=1$, use the opposite diagonal block. It introduces one crossing of sign $hv=-1$. The listed ten-grid is precisely these ten corner blocks, and its component cycle visits rows $0,4,9,2,7,1,5,8,3,6,0$, hence it is one knot. Away from the exceptional block it follows two blackboard parallel copies of the trefoil. The blackboard longitude has linking number equal to writhe $+3$, so $\lambda_{\mathrm{bb}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{pref}}+3\mu$. The one negative half-twist therefore gives slope $2\lambda_{\mathrm{bb}}-\mu=2\lambda_{\mathrm{pref}}+5\mu$, with longitudinal orientation inherited from the original trefoil. This is exactly $T_{2,3;2,5}$ in the Statement; it is not identified from a polynomial or a candidate matrix.

Compute the tilde groups of these three new grids by the following finite exact procedure. Enumerate the $n!$ state permutations $p$. For each ordered pair $a\ne b$, take the positive cyclic row interval $a\to b$ and column interval $p(a)\to p(b)$. Its initial corners are southwest and northeast, and the two row orders give the two directed rectangles for each unordered pair. Retain the rectangle exactly when its cell support contains no $O$ or $X$, and no state point lies in the product of its strict interior intervals. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Let $C^-(K)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by $U^n x_r$ for $n\ge0$, with $M(U^n x_r)=M(x_r)-2n$ and $A(U^n x_r)=A(x_r)-n$, and assume $H_*(C^-(K))\cong\mathbb F_2[U]$ with generator in Maslov degree zero. $$ 0\le \nu^-(K)\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K), $$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball bounded by $K$.

$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. $$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.

For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, the function $\Upsilon_K:[0,2]\to\mathbb R$ defined by the finite cycle minimax is continuous and piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints, satisfies $\Upsilon_K(0)=0$ and $\Upsilon_K(t)=\Upsilon_K(2-t)$, and has right derivative $\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\tau(K)$. For smooth oriented knots $K,J$ and $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_{K\#J}(t)=\Upsilon_K(t)+\Upsilon_J(t),\qquad \Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $-K$ is the reverse mirror, the inverse under connected sum in the smooth concordance group. If $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth properly embedded compact connected oriented surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then
$$ |\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)\qquad(0\le t\le1). $$

Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B$, then $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.

The invariant satisfies $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$, $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules
$$ \epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(K),\qquad \epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(J). $$
The converse of $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\tau=0$ and $\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\epsilon=1$, not $2$.

Let $K,J\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots that cobound a smooth properly embedded annulus in $S^3\times[0,1]$. Then there are finite-rank free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ bifiltered chain complexes $A$ and $B$ with zero total homology such that
$$ \mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A\simeq\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B, $$
where $\simeq$ denotes a Maslov-graded chain homotopy equivalence whose maps and chain homotopies do not increase either filtration. The complexes $A$ and $B$ are acyclic after the filtrations are forgotten; they need not be acyclic in either associated-graded complex.

Stable-equivalence invariance in [F3] then gives $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$, so epsilon is well-defined on $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}$. Work over $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ chain complex with Maslov grading $M$ and bifiltration coordinates $(i,j)$. Multiplication by $U$ lowers each filtration coordinate by one and lowers $M$ by two; the differential lowers $M$ by one and does not increase either filtration. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with its generator normalized in Maslov grading zero.

For a filtration region $R$, write $C\{R\}$ for the corresponding subquotient of the bifiltered complex; in particular $C\{i=0\}$ is the vertical complex, $C\{j=s\}$ is the horizontal complex at Alexander level $s$, and $C\{i=0,j\le s\}$ is the subcomplex of the vertical complex at levels at most $s$. Define
$$ \tau(C)=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z: H_*(C\{i=0,j\le s\})\longrightarrow H_*(C\{i=0\})\text{ is nonzero} \}. $$
For each integer $s$, let $F_s$ be the homology map induced by the chain map from $C\{i=0\}$ to $C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i=0,j<s\}$ and then including the quotient. Let $G_s$ be the homology map from $C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$ to $C\{i=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i<0,j=s\}$ and then including. The epsilon invariant is
$$ \epsilon(C)=\begin{cases} 1,&F_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ -1,&G_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ 0,&F_{\tau(C)}\ne0\text{ and }G_{\tau(C)}\ne0. \end{cases} $$
Here zero and nonzero refer to the induced homology maps. This definition fixes the sign convention; invariance under stable equivalence is a separate claim.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B$, then $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.

The invariant satisfies $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$, $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules
$$ \epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(K),\qquad \epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(J). $$
The converse of $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\tau=0$ and $\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\epsilon=1$, not $2$.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Let $G$ be any $n\times n$ grid diagram representing a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$. Form the diagonal grid complex by setting every marking variable $U_i$ equal to a single variable $U$, and define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ by the t-modified non-torsion grading on that complex for $0\le t\le1$, extended by $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$ for $1<t\le2$. Then for every $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $\Upsilon_K$ is the finite cycle-minimax invariant defined from $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$. In this statement the quotient with all $U_i$ identified carries the factor $W^{\otimes(n-1)}$, where $W$ has generators in Maslov/Alexander bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$; this factor is retained in the proof and is not counted as an improvement to the grid-state complexity bound.

derivations.claim: In the vertical complex, the differential is $x_1\mapsto x_2$, so its degree-zero homology generator is $x_0$ and first appears at Alexander level $1$. The normalized comparison in [F4], after quotient by the chosen $U$ action, identifies this filtered hat complex with the specified-data complex in [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]]; hence $\tau(T_{2,3})=1$. For the exact epsilon maps at $s=1$, the target of $F_1$ contains $U^{-1}x_1$ with boundary $x_0$: its other differential term $U^{-1}x_2$ has $j<1$ and is killed there. Thus $F_1=0$. The source of $G_1$ contains the degree-zero cycle $x_0$, while $U^{-1}x_1$ has $i>0$ and is excluded, so that class survives and maps to the nonzero vertical class. Thus $G_1\ne0$ and the exact three-case definition gives epsilon $1$ for this complex.

A Maslov-zero cycle representing the normalized total generator is either $x_0$ or $U^{-1}x_2$: the Maslov-zero chain group in the displayed basis is spanned by these two cycles, and $\partial(U^{-1}x_1)=x_0+U^{-1}x_2$ makes their homology classes equal. Their coordinates are $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$, so their filtration levels are $t/2$ and $1-t/2$. Therefore $\nu_t=\min(t/2,1-t/2)$ and $\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)=-2\nu_t$, which gives the stated two linear pieces. They agree at $t=1$, where the slope changes.

The algebraic Laurent dual of the displayed complex has generators $x_0^*,x_1^*,x_2^*$ at Maslov/Alexander values $(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$ and differential $\partial x_0^*=Ux_1^*$, $\partial x_2^*=x_1^*$, $\partial x_1^*=0$. In its vertical complex $x_2^*$ maps to $x_1^*$, leaving $x_0^*$ as generator at Alexander level $-1$. At $s=-1$, the $F_{-1}$ target kills $Ux_1^*$ because $i<0$, so $x_0^*$ becomes a cycle; its only degree-one basis vector is $x_1^*$ with zero differential, so the class is not a boundary and $F_{-1}\ne0$. The $G_{-1}$ source has only $x_0^*$ in degree zero, and its differential $Ux_1^*$ is retained; $Ux_2^*$ lies above $j=-1$ and is excluded. Hence $G_{-1}=0$ and the exact epsilon convention gives $-1$. The degree-zero chain space has basis $x_0^*,Ux_2^*$; their individual differentials are both $Ux_1^*$, so the only nonzero cycle is $x_0^*+Ux_2^*$, and it represents the normalized generator. Its two terms have coordinates $(0,-1)$ and $(-1,0)$, giving $\nu_t^*=\max(-t/2,-1+t/2)=-\min(t/2,1-t/2)$. Thus its Upsilon is the negative of the value in step 1.2 by an explicit cycle computation. Fact [F3] identifies the dual of an ADMITTED knot complex with its actual reverse-mirror complex. Both numerical knot-level values here still require admission of this specific staircase from an actual trefoil diagram.

Under [F5], the same calculation is obtained from the diagonal grid complex after accounting for its $W^{\otimes(n-1)}$ factors, whose nonzero t-grade shifts are nonpositive on $[0,1]$. The factor is retained and does not change the maximal non-torsion grading.
